newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker rates drop, despite fixing.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker rates drop, despite fixing.

text.p: Crude tanker rates in the key Middle East Gulf market plummeted on Tuesday, despite good fixing activity over the last few days.
Although no ULCC charters were seen out of the Middle East five VLCCs found employment, but the respectable chartering level failed to stop rates dropping.
"Rates in the Mideast Gulf have dropped particularly on the AG-West route. There is an over abundance of tonnage," said one shipbroker.
Three VLCCs were seen heading Eastwards, with MOC taking a 250,000 tonne cargo on the Samco Europe to Japan. Both Petrobras and Fina chartered VLCCs to Brazil and the UKC respectively.
Tankers bound for the U.S and Europe were assessed at W55, a fall of five worldscale points, brokers said.
Fina's chartering of the 262,000 tonner, Rome, travelling from Kharg Island to the UKC at W55 was seen to reflect the market.
Shipping brokers said VLCC rates Eastwards were knocked lower with Japanese destinations taking W65 from W70 last week.
West African chartering was seen to have the most steady rates with 250,000 tonners travelling to the U.S. Gulf around W65.
In the Mediterranean, chartering consolidated on last week's late upturn, but despite the increase in business 80,000 tonners making cross Med trips were still restricted to W100-102.5.
Turkey's Tupras were seen taking a 80,000 tonne cargo on the Cerda travelling from Banias to Turkey at a high W127.5, but brokers did not feel this reflected the market.
In the inter-UKC sector rates on 80,000 tonners were steady around W100 .

Rumours circled that Sinochem intend to take a VLCC from West Coast Norway to Rijeka around the 12th of September and that Vitol may be chartering a VLCC of Brent to the USG also causing a stir. But there was no confirmation as yet to either enquiry.
The Caribbean market saw rates largely settle around last done levels, North American brokers said. 70,000 tonners travelling up the U.S coast were steady around W130.
